loading_technique: R/weights-shape.R and R/offset.R are fully sys.source()-loaded (proven side-effect-free by the already-retained 56-case tools/core070_data_controls.R run); only the single top-level `miss_control <- function(...)` assignment is cherry-picked out of R/gllvmTMB.R by parsing it and eval()-ing just that one expression, exactly as tools/core070_data_controls.R already does. No installed package, model fit, TMB object, or Julia code runs.
julia_surface_status: GLLVM.jl has no public or internal surface for any of the four helpers exercised here: no MissingDataControl/miss_control-equivalent constructor, no formula-offset-term evaluator with count-family admission, no stored-training-offset or predict-time-offset accessor on a fit object, and no normalise_weights-equivalent (long/wide_matrix/wide_df, with masking) weight adapter. tools/core070_data_batch.jl checks this at runtime against the loaded GLLVM module (isdefined() over named candidates, plus Base.kwarg_decl() over gllvm()/fit_gllvm() to rule out an undocumented keyword) rather than resting on this claim alone. Every one of the 28 required cases is therefore bound only to the frozen R replay: verdict SPEC_DEFECT, not a defect in the specs -- the annex itself describes each julia_surface as planned, not implemented. This is the same situation, and the same resolution, as docs/dev-log/core070/isdm-batch-contract.json's julia_surface_status for the sibling isdm area.

cases.r_call: miss_control('include','model') (test/parity/fixtures/core070_data_controls.R#DATA-MISS-BOTH); expected response='include', predictor='model', engine='laplace'.
cases.julia_surface: Julia control constructor must accept both response and predictor overrides simultaneously while leaving engine at its default.
cases.rationale: Joint-override case closing out the miss_control() default/override family alongside DATA-MISS-DEFAULT/INCLUDE/MODEL.

cases.r_call: miss_control() from frozen R source (test/parity/fixtures/core070_data_controls.R#DATA-MISS-DEFAULT); expected list(response='drop', predictor='fail', engine='laplace').
cases.julia_surface: Julia missing-data control constructor (planned: e.g. MissingDataControl() or the fit()-level miss= keyword default) must expose the same three defaults: response drop, predictor fail, engine laplace.
cases.rationale: Pure default-value contract with no Julia counterpart yet; a public fit()-facing control object or keyword set must reproduce these three defaults before the family/data-handling manifest can close.

cases.r_call: miss_control(response='include') (test/parity/fixtures/core070_data_controls.R#DATA-MISS-INCLUDE); expected response='include' with predictor/engine defaults unchanged.
cases.julia_surface: Julia control constructor must accept an independent response=override (e.g. :include) leaving predictor/engine defaults untouched.
cases.rationale: Single-argument override case for the same control object; verifies argument independence, not just the all-defaults case.

cases.r_call: miss_control(predictor='model') (test/parity/fixtures/core070_data_controls.R#DATA-MISS-MODEL); expected predictor='model' with response/engine defaults unchanged.
cases.julia_surface: Julia control constructor must accept an independent predictor=override (e.g. :model) leaving response/engine defaults untouched.
cases.rationale: Single-argument override case complementary to DATA-MISS-INCLUDE; together they pin that the two axes are independently settable.

cases.r_call: gll_prepare_offset(quote(e), c(5L,10L,11L), ...) (test/parity/fixtures/core070_data_controls.R#DATA-OFF-ALL-COUNT); expected c(1,2,4) -- nonzero offset admitted for count family ids 5/10/11.
cases.julia_surface: Julia offset-preparation surface must admit a nonzero offset for every count-family id in its family registry (the ids paired to 5/10/11 in R's internal family table), rejecting others per DATA-OFF-NONCOUNT-REJECT.
cases.rationale: Family-id admission-set case; the Julia family registry's numeric ids differ from R's, so the comparand is the *set of families admitted* (count families), not the literal integer ids -- flagged uncertain only insofar as the id-to-family mapping needs to be pinned once at case-authoring time, not deferred as a separate obligation.

cases.r_call: gll_prepare_offset(quote(log(e)), ...) (test/parity/fixtures/core070_data_controls.R#DATA-OFF-EXPOSURE); expected log(c(1,2,4)) -- log-exposure offset evaluated per row from data.
cases.julia_surface: Julia offset-preparation surface must evaluate a data-column offset expression (log-exposure) row-wise against the training data frame.
cases.rationale: The canonical count-model exposure-offset case (formula `offset(log(e))`); required before any Poisson/NB exposure workflow can be claimed.

cases.r_call: gll_prepare_offset(quote(c(1,0,4)), c(2L,0L,5L), ...) (test/parity/fixtures/core070_data_controls.R#DATA-OFF-MIXED); expected c(1,0,4) -- a multi-family fit with mixed family ids per row permits zero offset on non-count rows alongside nonzero on count rows.
cases.julia_surface: Julia offset-preparation surface must apply the per-row family-id admission rule row-wise within a single multi-family/multi-response fit, not just at the whole-model level.
cases.rationale: Row-wise variant of the family-conditioned offset rule; required for any multi-response/multi-family model where offsets and family ids vary by column.

cases.r_call: gll_prepare_offset(quote(e), rep(15L,3), ...) (test/parity/fixtures/core070_data_controls.R#DATA-OFF-NB1); expected c(1,2,4) -- NB1 (family id 15) also admits a nonzero offset.
cases.julia_surface: Julia offset-preparation surface must admit a nonzero offset for the NB1 family specifically (a count family outside the {5,10,11} block tested in DATA-OFF-ALL-COUNT).
cases.rationale: Regression-style case isolating NB1 from the other count-family ids; keeps the admission set from silently narrowing to {5,10,11}.

cases.r_call: gll_prepare_offset(quote(0), rep(0L,3), ...) (test/parity/fixtures/core070_data_controls.R#DATA-OFF-NONCOUNT-ZERO); expected rep(0,3) -- an explicit all-zero offset is accepted for a non-count family (offset ids all 0).
cases.julia_surface: Julia offset-preparation surface must accept an explicit zero offset for non-count families rather than rejecting the offset() term outright.
comparands: R zero offset on non-count family
Julia zero offset on non-count family
cases.rationale: Pairs with DATA-OFF-NONCOUNT-REJECT (non-zero offset on non-count family rejects); this row is the accepted boundary at zero.

cases.r_call: gll_prepare_offset(NULL, ...) via off(NULL) (test/parity/fixtures/core070_data_controls.R#DATA-OFF-NONE); expected rep(0,3) -- absent offset defaults to zero per row.
cases.julia_surface: Julia offset-preparation surface (planned: prepare_offset()/offset handling inside the family fit driver) must default an absent offset expression to a zero vector of length n_obs.
cases.rationale: Baseline no-offset case anchoring the offset-preparation contract; every other DATA-OFF-* row is a variant of this same helper.

cases.r_call: .gllvmTMB_offset_newdata(fit, d) (test/parity/fixtures/core070_data_controls.R#DATA-OFF-PREDICT); expected log(c(1,2,4)) -- the stored offset expression (log(e)) is re-evaluated against new data at predict time.
cases.julia_surface: Julia predict()-time offset handling must re-evaluate the fit's stored offset expression against the supplied newdata rather than reusing the training offset vector.
cases.rationale: Core predict-time offset contract; required before any offset-bearing count-family predict() workflow can be claimed against R.

cases.r_call: .gllvmTMB_offset_newdata(fit, data.frame(e=c(0,1,2))) (test/parity/fixtures/core070_data_controls.R#DATA-OFF-PREDICT-NONFINITE-HELPER); expected c(-Inf,0,log(2)) -- log(0) passes through as -Inf at this helper (no guard at newdata-offset level).
cases.julia_surface: Julia predict-time offset evaluator must reproduce the same unguarded arithmetic (log(0) = -Inf propagates rather than erroring) at this specific helper, matching R's documented non-guard here -- any stronger Julia diagnostic must be an explicit, separately tested design choice, not an accidental behavioral divergence.
cases.rationale: Deliberately documents a permissive R behavior (source comment: 'this differs from training validation'); Julia may choose to guard here, but the divergence must be an explicit tested decision, so this row is required to make that choice visible rather than silent.

cases.r_call: gll_prepare_offset(quote(log(2)), ...) (test/parity/fixtures/core070_data_controls.R#DATA-OFF-SCALAR); expected rep(log(2),3) -- a constant expression broadcasts to all rows.
cases.julia_surface: Julia offset-preparation surface must broadcast a constant offset expression/value to a per-row vector of the training length.
cases.rationale: Confirms scalar-expression broadcasting, distinct from the per-row exposure case (DATA-OFF-EXPOSURE).

cases.r_call: .gllvmTMB_offset_vec(fit) with no stored offset_vec (test/parity/fixtures/core070_data_controls.R#DATA-OFF-TRAIN-LEGACY); expected rep(0,3) -- fits from before offset_vec was cached fall back to zero.
cases.julia_surface: Julia's stored-fit offset accessor (planned: offset(fit) or an internal training-offset getter) must return an all-zero vector when the fit object predates offset caching, matching R's legacy fallback.
cases.rationale: Back-compatibility fallback for fit objects saved before offset caching existed; a Julia serialization/versioning story must define the equivalent fallback before this can close.

cases.r_call: .gllvmTMB_offset_vec(fit) with tmb_data$offset_vec set (test/parity/fixtures/core070_data_controls.R#DATA-OFF-TRAIN-STORED); expected the stored vector c(1,2,3) verbatim.
cases.julia_surface: Julia's stored-fit offset accessor must return the cached training offset vector unchanged when the fit object carries one.
cases.rationale: Positive counterpart to DATA-OFF-TRAIN-LEGACY; together they pin the stored-vs-fallback offset contract on a fitted model object.

cases.r_call: normalise_weights(c(10,20),'wide_df',4L,mask) via w(c(10,20),'wide_df',4L,mask) (test/parity/fixtures/core070_data_controls.R#DATA-W-DF-MASK-DROP); expected c(10,10,20,20) -- traits()-route masked cells dropped, trait-major retained order.
cases.julia_surface: Julia native trait-major weight input must drop masked cells under drop_masked=true, matching R's traits()-route retained order.
comparands: Julia native trait-major masked-drop weight vector
cases.rationale: Mask-drop variant of DATA-W-DF-UNIT; direct native reproduction, no adapter transpose needed since this route already matches Julia's trait-major storage.

cases.r_call: normalise_weights(c(10,20),'wide_df',6L,mask,FALSE) via w(c(10,20),'wide_df',6L,mask,FALSE) (test/parity/fixtures/core070_data_controls.R#DATA-W-DF-MASK-INCLUDE); expected c(10,10,10,20,20,20) -- with drop_masked=FALSE the traits()-route weight at a masked cell is RETAINED (not zeroed), unlike the wide-matrix masked-include case.
cases.julia_surface: Julia native trait-major weight input in masked-include mode must retain the per-unit weight value at masked cells rather than zeroing it -- this differs from the wide-matrix masked-include contract (DATA-W-MATRIX-MASK-INCLUDE zeros; this route does not) and both behaviors must be reproduced distinctly, not collapsed to one rule.
comparands: R traits()-route masked-include weight vector (retained, not zeroed)
Julia native trait-major masked-include weight vector (retained)
cases.rationale: Contract explicitly distinguishes this from the wide-matrix masked-include row per data-controls-contract.md ('Site weights retained at masked entries' for traits() vs 'Masked entries zeroed' for the matrix route) -- a real behavioral asymmetry, not a documentation artifact, so both must be separately verified.

cases.r_call: normalise_weights(c(10,20), shape='wide_df') via w(c(10,20),'wide_df') (test/parity/fixtures/core070_data_controls.R#DATA-W-DF-UNIT); expected c(10,10,10,20,20,20) -- the traits()-route per-unit weight broadcasts in trait-major order.
cases.julia_surface: Julia's native traits()-style weight input (trait-major, matching Julia's own binomial-N storage order per the data-controls contract) must broadcast a per-unit weight vector to c(10,10,10,20,20,20) -- the SAME order as Julia's native layout, unlike the wide-matrix route.
cases.rationale: This is the order that already matches Julia's native trait-major layout (per data-controls-contract.md); evidence_kind is native (direct reproduction), contrasting with the wide-matrix rows which are bridge/adapter cases.

cases.r_call: normalise_weights(rep(0.5,6), ...) via w(rep(0.5,6)) (test/parity/fixtures/core070_data_controls.R#DATA-W-FRACTIONAL); expected rep(0.5,6) -- fractional weights are accepted at this helper.
cases.julia_surface: Julia weight-normalisation surface must accept fractional weight values without erroring; family-specific trial-count validation (e.g. binomial N must be integer) happens elsewhere.
cases.rationale: Companion to DATA-W-ZERO; both pin the same deliberate-permissiveness contract for weight values at this layer.

cases.r_call: normalise_weights(1:6, shape='long') via w(1:6) (test/parity/fixtures/core070_data_controls.R#DATA-W-LONG); expected as.numeric(1:6) -- an exact-length long vector passes through unchanged.
cases.julia_surface: Julia weight-normalisation surface must accept an exact-length long weight vector and return it unchanged (no reordering).
cases.rationale: Identity case for the long-vector input route.

cases.r_call: normalise_weights(matrix(1:6,2,3), shape='wide_matrix') via w(matrix(1:6,2,3),'wide_matrix') (test/parity/fixtures/core070_data_controls.R#DATA-W-MATRIX-CELLS); expected as.numeric(1:6) -- a full units x traits weight matrix flattens column-major (R's native matrix storage order).
cases.julia_surface: Julia wide-matrix weight adapter must accept a full per-cell weight matrix and flatten/transpose it to Julia's native trait-major storage, matching the general per-cell case of the DATA-W-MATRIX-UNIT ordering contract.
comparands: R full per-cell weight matrix (column-major flatten)
Julia native per-cell weight layout after adapter transpose
cases.rationale: General per-cell case of the same ordering contract as DATA-W-MATRIX-UNIT; required so the adapter is verified beyond the constant-per-unit special case.

cases.r_call: normalise_weights(wm,'wide_matrix',4L,mask) via w(wm,'wide_matrix',4L,mask) (test/parity/fixtures/core070_data_controls.R#DATA-W-MATRIX-MASK-DROP); expected c(1,2,4,5) -- masked (NA-response) cells are dropped, shrinking the returned vector to n_obs actually retained.
cases.julia_surface: Julia wide-matrix weight adapter must drop weights at cells masked out by a missing/NA response (drop_masked=true default), returning a vector of length equal to the retained-observation count, in the adapter's native flatten order.
cases.rationale: Mask-drop variant of the wide-matrix ordering contract; required for any model with response missingness under the response='drop' default (DATA-MISS-DEFAULT).

cases.r_call: normalise_weights(wm,'wide_matrix',6L,mask,FALSE) via w(wm,'wide_matrix',6L,mask,FALSE) (test/parity/fixtures/core070_data_controls.R#DATA-W-MATRIX-MASK-INCLUDE); expected c(1,2,0,4,5,0) -- with drop_masked=FALSE, masked cells are retained in place and zeroed rather than dropped.
cases.julia_surface: Julia wide-matrix weight adapter must support a masked-include mode (drop_masked=false, paired with miss_control(response='include') from DATA-MISS-INCLUDE) that zeros masked cells in place instead of shrinking the vector.
comparands: R masked-include weight vector (zero-filled, full length 6)
cases.rationale: Companion to DATA-W-MATRIX-MASK-DROP for the response='include' path; both modes must be supported since miss_control's response policy is user-selectable (DATA-MISS-INCLUDE/BOTH).

cases.r_call: normalise_weights(2,'wide_matrix',4L,mask) via w(2,'wide_matrix',4L,mask) (test/parity/fixtures/core070_data_controls.R#DATA-W-MATRIX-MASK-SCALAR); expected rep(2,4) -- a scalar weight broadcasts only to the retained (unmasked) cells under drop_masked=TRUE.
cases.julia_surface: Julia wide-matrix weight adapter must broadcast a scalar weight to exactly the retained-observation count when combined with masking, not to the full unmasked cell count.
comparands: R scalar broadcast restricted to unmasked cells (length 4)
Julia scalar broadcast restricted to unmasked cells
cases.rationale: Interaction case between scalar broadcast (DATA-W-MATRIX-SCALAR) and masking (DATA-W-MATRIX-MASK-DROP); confirms the two rules compose correctly rather than being tested only in isolation.

cases.r_call: normalise_weights(2, shape='wide_matrix') via w(2,'wide_matrix') (test/parity/fixtures/core070_data_controls.R#DATA-W-MATRIX-SCALAR); expected rep(2,6) -- a scalar broadcasts to every units*traits cell.
cases.julia_surface: Julia wide-matrix weight-normalisation surface must broadcast a scalar weight to every cell of the units*traits response matrix, flattened in the same order as the unmasked case.
cases.rationale: Scalar-broadcast case for the wide-matrix input route.

cases.r_call: normalise_weights(c(10,20), shape='wide_matrix') via w(c(10,20),'wide_matrix') (test/parity/fixtures/core070_data_controls.R#DATA-W-MATRIX-UNIT); expected c(10,20,10,20,10,20) -- R units x traits matrix order (site-major).
cases.julia_surface: Julia's wide-matrix weight adapter must reproduce R's units x traits (site-major) flattening order for a per-unit weight vector; per the data-controls contract, Julia's own native binomial N is traits x units (trait-major, matching DATA-W-DF-UNIT order), so a wide-matrix *adapter* into that native layout must transpose -- this case pins the R-side order the adapter must read from.
comparands: Julia wide-matrix-adapter input order before transpose to native trait-major layout
cases.rationale: This is the ordering-contract row called out explicitly in data-controls-contract.md ('Julia native binomial N is traits x units ... A matrix adapter must transpose the R units x traits matrix'); evidence_kind is bridge because the comparand is an R->Julia adapter transform, not a same-order native reproduction.

cases.r_call: normalise_weights(NULL, ...) via w(NULL) (test/parity/fixtures/core070_data_controls.R#DATA-W-NULL); expected NULL.
cases.julia_surface: Julia weight-normalisation surface (planned: normalise_weights()/the weights= handling inside fit()) must pass NULL/absent weights through unchanged (equivalent to `nothing` or unweighted fit).
cases.rationale: Baseline no-weights case anchoring the weight-normalisation contract; every other DATA-W-* row is a variant of this same helper.

cases.r_call: normalise_weights(rep(0,6), ...) via w(rep(0,6)) (test/parity/fixtures/core070_data_controls.R#DATA-W-ZERO); expected rep(0,6) -- all-zero weights are accepted at this helper (not validated as a degenerate fit here).
cases.julia_surface: Julia weight-normalisation surface must accept an all-zero weight vector without erroring; any degenerate-fit rejection belongs at a later fit-time validation stage, not this shape/policy helper.
cases.rationale: Pins that weight-value validation (zero, fractional) is deliberately permissive at this layer, matching R's documented separation of concerns from family-specific validation.

cases.r_call: normalise_weights(1:6,shape='long') compared against a deliberately wrong literal c(9,9,9,9,9,9)
cases.julia_surface: n/a -- negative control, R-side only
cases.rationale: Must evaluate to FALSE: the real result (1,2,3,4,5,6) does not equal the wrong literal. If this ever reports TRUE, the identical()-based comparison used throughout this batch is broken (e.g. silently coerced to always-pass) and every other PASS in this batch is untrustworthy.

cases.r_call: normalise_weights(c(10,20),shape='wide_matrix') compared against the reversed order c(20,10,20,10,20,10)
cases.julia_surface: n/a -- negative control, R-side only
cases.rationale: Must evaluate to FALSE: the real R units-by-traits order is (10,20,10,20,10,20), not its reverse. This is the exact same case data-controls-contract.md cites as the one whose expected-value mutation must flip a batch from all-pass to one-fail; reproducing that here pins that this batch's comparison is equally sensitive to an ordering error, not just a magnitude error.

failure_action: Retain the complete attempt (results JSON, raw.tsv, diagnostics.log, receipt.json, the Julia introspection receipt). Do not widen the exact identical()-based comparison to a tolerance or a substring match, and do not drop a failing case from expected_case_count.
claim_boundary: Passing this batch establishes that the frozen R helper behaviour for these 28 manifest-planned data cases replays correctly, in isolation, against the pinned R source at the reference commit, and that no Julia surface currently exists to compare any of them against (a fact, not a gap in this harness). It does not establish any Julia native/formula/bridge fit, any numeric R-vs-Julia parity, or admission behaviour for the 28 non-manifest reject/error cases in the wider 56-case docs/dev-log/core070/data-controls-subset.json. The family/data-handling manifest cannot close on this evidence alone; it closes only once the planned Julia surfaces above are implemented and a follow-up batch replaces every SPEC_DEFECT verdict with a real R-vs-Julia value comparison.
